newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices fall on new crop arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices fall on new crop arrivals.

text.p: Indian cotton prices fell on Wednesday on lower demand from mills and state firms while rising new crop arrivals kept sentiment down, dealers said.

Daily new crop arrivals in the Punjab region has risen to 30-35,000 bales (170 kg each). In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned fell by 30/50 rupees to 1,420/1,580 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi fell by 25/35 rupees to 810/830 rupees.
Gujarat cotton was unchanged. Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) remained steady at 17,000/18,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
"Closing sentiment was subdued in the absence of any move by the government to allow more cotton exports," one broker said.
